subject: Can I use methylkit to test for differences in a specific region of a chromosome?

messages.author: 04cd5e94675bf57b
messages.subject: Can I use methylkit to test for differences in a specific region of a chromosome?
parts:
Hi
I have a question, not sure how naive it may be.
I have a region upstream a gene on bovine chromosome 6 that I would like to see if there is differential methylation between two groups.
When running the analysis for all my data, nothing on chromosome 6 showed up as hyper or hypo methylated.
But I would like to check if there is any difference at all in that region (even if not that statistically signifcant).
My question is that if I can supply the coordinates for that region into methylkit and run an analysis on just that region?

Thank you!

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Can I use methylkit to test for differences in a specific region of a chromosome?
parts:
yes, you can. You need to subset the locations in methylKit objects and run analysis. You can also look at the bulk analysis, a methylDiff object containing all positions and check methylation differences on the region of your interest, for that purpose you can then ignore q-values and p-values. 

Best,
Altuna
